nodes.title: Oak
nodes.markdown:
# Oak Welcome! Oak is our **Unitree Go2**, a lower-cost robot dog that normally walks wherever its hand remote tells it. This repo is **Team 48's** software for Oak, built with **ROS 2 Humble** (a toolkit where small programs, called *nodes*, pass data on named channels, called *topics*). It grows out of the open-source [go2_ros2_sdk](https://github.com/abizovnuralem/go2_ros2_sdk) project; go there for upstream support. ## Why we're building it Our end goal is **autonomous mapping**: Oak moves on its own, with no one holding the controller. Real service dogs are very expensive. A robot dog that costs about $3,000 and has computer vision could do some of that work, like guiding a blind person and talking to them through earbuds. **Our milestone now:** Oak maps and explores a room by itself. ## What Oak can do today - Stream its camera, lidar (a spinning laser that measures distance) and joint positions to your laptop over Wi-Fi. - Show all of it live in RViz, a 3D viewer. - Drive from the keyboard, a gamepad, or RViz buttons, with a referee (twist_mux) deciding who is in charge. - Spot objects like people and chairs with YOLO computer vision.

## The map This page is the center of the wiki. Each hub links to one page per program. ```mermaid graph LR Oak((Oak)) Oak --- Driving Oak --- Driver Oak --- Senses Oak --- MapsNav[Maps & Nav] Oak --- Brains Oak --- Lab[Lab setup] Oak --- Team ``` - [Driving](docs/wiki/driving.md): keyboard, gamepad, RViz panels, and twist_mux, the referee. - [Driver](docs/wiki/driver.md): the one program that talks to the real robot, over Wi-Fi or Ethernet. - [Senses](docs/wiki/senses.md): lidar, camera, computer vision, and TF (tracking where each body part is). - [Maps & Nav](docs/wiki/maps-nav.md): SLAM (building a map while locating yourself on it), Nav2 (path planning), the auto mapper, map viewers. - [Brains](docs/wiki/brains.md): the AI agent that turns sentences into actions, walking to objects, and voice. - [Lab setup](docs/wiki/lab-setup.md): Docker, WSL, the lab checklist, and the robot test log. - [Team](docs/wiki/team.md): roadmap, decisions, and who's who. ## Get set up **You need:** a laptop with Docker Desktop and about 16 GB of RAM. Windows users also need WSL2 (Linux inside Windows). Macs work too. You do **not** need the robot. Everything runs inside **Docker**, which packs all the software into one identical box (a *container*), so nothing gets installed on your machine. 1. **Get the code and build** (the first build takes about 15 minutes, so start it and keep reading): ```shell git clone --recursive git@github.com:maxhawksby/go2-fusion.git cd go2-fusion/docker docker compose build docker compose run --rm unitree_ros true # builds every package, then exits ``` 2. **Try a dry run.** Open a container shell and start the keyboard driver: ```shell docker compose run --rm --name oak-dry unitree_ros bash teleop ``` In a second terminal, watch what it sends. Hold W and the forward speed appears; let go and a stop follows. ```shell docker exec -it oak-dry bash -ic 'ros2 topic echo /cmd_vel_keyboard' ``` 3. **Meet the real Oak** in the lab, with a teammate, using the lab checklist. Ask a teammate for access details; they are never in this repo. 4. **Pick a task** from GitHub issues (see below), make a branch, and open a pull request. Windows without WSL, Macs, memory errors, and RViz windows: see [Lab setup](docs/wiki/lab-setup.md). ## What we're working on now (week of Oct 18) - **Auto mapper** (Luis): reliable exploration. Fixed false walls caused by floor drift, added Scan and Reset maps buttons in RViz, and made frontier search faster. *Next:* full exploration tests on Oak. - **Text-to-speech** (Jeth, reviewed by Noah): Piper, a local voice, speaking through Oak's speaker. The audio is choppy and drops the start of short clips. *Next:* fix the packet loss, then connect it to voice commands. - **AI agent** (Adib): Ollama runs a local Qwen model in place of the paid OpenAI API, and a fast local parser handles common commands. *Next:* odometry and turn accuracy. - **Oak Control dashboard** (Noah): a dashboard plus a ROS 2 bridge, showing live sensors and detections over WebRTC and Foxglove. - **Computer vision** (Max): YOLO object detection that remembers where objects are, to help map rooms. **Open issues from the last robot test:** 1. Retest Nav2 goals and click-to-walk in the map viewer. 2. Retest how keyboard driving feels after the teleop fixes. 3. Find what starts the lidar-to-pointcloud node and check its input topic. 4. Confirm by eye that Oak stops cleanly when a driver goes quiet. **Tasks live as GitHub issues**, labelled `wiki:` (for example `wiki:maps-nav`). Take one by assigning it to yourself. ## Team and how we work Max Hawksby, Luis (LuisMend12), Noah Steinberg, Adib Rouf, and Jeth. TODO(Max): each person's role, Luis's full name, and confirm Jeth is GitHub user jevgome. - **Branches are your sandbox.** Push whatever you like; no review needed. - **Merging into `master`** needs one teammate's approval and green automatic checks. - **Keep the wiki true:** if you change a program's code, update its wiki page in the same pull request. - Test without the robot first. There is one Oak and it accepts one connection at a time. - Never commit keys, passwords, or lab Wi-Fi details. ## Credits and license Built on [go2_ros2_sdk](https://github.com/abizovnuralem/go2_ros2_sdk) by @abizovnuralem, using [@tfoldi](https://github.com/tfoldi)'s [go2-webrtc](https://github.com/tfoldi/go2-webrtc), with thanks to its contributors and the TheRoboVerse community. Includes Riley Francis's [ROS2-LLM-Nav](https://github.com/RileyFrancis/ROS2-LLM-Nav) and [J. Francis's COCO detector](https://github.com/jfrancis71/ros2_coco_detector). BSD 2-clause License. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

nodes.title: Brains
nodes.markdown:
# Brains

The higher-level behaviour: plain-English commands, walking to objects, voice and posture.

Part of: [Oak](../../README.md)

## Pages

- [LLM agent](llm-agent.md) - Turns plain-English commands into robot actions; built by Riley on GPT-4o-mini and being rebuilt on Claude, so it builds but does not run yet.
- [Object navigation](object-navigation.md) - Walks toward an object that object detection has seen (`/navigate_to_object`), on twist_mux priority 3; it has no obstacle avoidance.
- [Voice](voice.md) - Speech in and out: `host_tools/speech_to_text` sends microphone transcripts to the LLM agent, and `speech_processor` speaks `/tts` through the robot's speaker.
- [Posture](posture.md) - Leg and posture commands: `sit_controller` sends a real Sit command, while `front_leg_controller` is still a placeholder.

# Driving

How people steer Oak by hand, and how every drive command is merged before it reaches the robot.

Part of: [Oak](../../README.md)

- [Keyboard teleop](keyboard-teleop.md) - Drives Oak from a terminal keyboard, publishing on `/cmd_vel_keyboard` (twist_mux priority 9) only while a key is held.

- [RViz panels](rviz-panels.md) - Three RViz plugin panels: a map viewer with click-to-navigate, an auto mapper panel and a keyboard teleop panel.
- [twist_mux](twist-mux.md) - Merges every drive source and forwards the highest-priority active one to the driver; each source has its own input topic.
